Anna (PM): Quick sync — we need to recalibrate RICE for the upcoming quarter. A few enterprise customers pushed for compliance/KMS + audit logs which increases effort but has high revenue impact. Can we align on a normalization approach by EOD Fri?

Jacob (Eng): Agree we can't treat effort the same across self-serve vs enterprise. Enterprise has hidden ops cost. Suggest adding a per-customer "operational multiplier" rather than inflating effort directly.

Sasha (Product Ops): @Jacob +1 on multiplier idea. Also propose we reweight Impact from 1.0 -> 1.5 for revenue-verified customers (to reflect sales pull). That reduces bias toward PLG features.

Mike (Data): I can run a sensitivity sweep. Quick peek at current scores (raw):
```
Feature                     Reach  Impact  Confidence  Effort  RICE
enterprise-kms              50     8       0.7         20      140
prefix-cache-optim          200    4       0.9         8       900
predictive-batching         120    6       0.8         12      480
audit-log-retention         30     7       0.6         10      126
```
This is using standard R*I/C / E.

Olivia (Design): Important to include "launch readiness" criteria in gating. Even if RICE pushes a customer ask up, we need checklist items: E2E tests, migration docs, and support runbook. Otherwise we get backlog churning.

Raj (Customer Eng): From customers — 2 big accounts need KMS+HIPAA scope by Oct. They are willing to sign a TPA but need a delivery timeline. This should count vs. generic "reach".

Anna (PM): Proposed combined approach:
- normalize effort via a 1.2-1.5 enterprise multiplier (applied to effort)
- adjust Impact upward by +25% for revenue-verified contract influence
- keep Confidence separate (don't nudge it unless we have direct data)
- require a "launch readiness" gate; unsatisfied -> push to backlog unless sponsor signs off

Sasha (Product Ops): I'll run normalization variants: multiplier=1.2,1.35,1.5 and produce rescore table + delta to rank. Want to see how many items flip top-10.

Mike (Data): I'll run the sweep and output a small CSV. Will also compute mean change and which features are brittle to weight changes.

Jacob (Eng): One caution: if we keep raising Impact for enterprise, we risk starving infra/perf investments that reduce unit cost. Can we add a small "platform amortization" credit to Effort (i.e., shared infra reduces per-feature effort)?

Olivia (Design): Good call. Platform amortization should be explicit so we still fund reliability/perf. Maybe a -10% effort credit for items that can reuse core runtime improvements.

Anna (PM): Nice compromise: enterprise multiplier on top of net effort after amortization. Sequence: compute base effort -> subtract platform credit if eligible -> apply enterprise multiplier.

prio-bot: Current top candidates (pre-rescore): prefix-cache-optim, predictive-batching, enterprise-kms, audit-log-retention.

Sasha (Product Ops): Action items: run rescore matrix + produce top-12 for review by Thurs COB. I'll tag owners.

Mike (Data): I'll attach a short notebook with sensitivity analysis and two visualizations: rank stability + score delta.

Anna (PM): Decision criteria for final pick: revenue influence, slashed time-to-value for large customers, and platform reuse score. If a feature meets all 3 -> auto canary prioritization.

Raj (Customer Eng): I'll confirm which customers are in "revenue-verified" bucket and share PoC timelines.

Jacob (Eng): I'll create a short tech note listing dependencies (KMS, K8s policy, migration path) so owners can estimate amortization eligibility.

Olivia (Design): I'll list the minimum launch-readiness checklist items for each candidate so Sasha can gate correctly.

Anna (PM): Thanks all. Quick thumbs: react with :thumbsup: if you're good with the approach, :thinking_face: if you have concerns. Target: final prioritized list by next Monday so we can ship commits to sales ASAP.

(27 replies expected)
